summary: Lewis County, WA lookout site: L-4 cab built 1931 by the Snoqualmie NF, staffed by state foresters, abandoned 1965; ruins and debris remain on the summit behind a gate.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1965; ruins and debris remain on the summit

access.note: Reached by Forest Service Road 71 to a private gate near Lookout Mountain. Willhite says the gate is open only part of the year. No current Forest Service listing found.

visit.trail_note: Three miles, maybe four, with about 1,000 feet of gain from the gate (Willhite); the original trail can be followed below the lookout

notes_for_editor: Built (1931), abandonment (1965) and the summit ruins are consistent across the register and two hobbyist pages. Staffing start differs: the register says staffed by 1953, Willhite says later in the 1950s. Gate status and road use come only from Willhite's undated page; no current Forest Service listing was found, so confirm with the Gifford Pinchot NF before publishing access. The record's height_m 3.0 is not a structure height in any source read; the washingtonlookouts NGS note describes a lookout house about 10 ft high, which may be where 3.0 m came from. Do not confuse with the Huckleberry Mountain at willhiteweb lookout_188 (a different peak, 5,472 ft summit) or with Little Huckleberry Mountain.
